title: `SUBSTR` wraps positions and lengths at 32 bits
verdict: a start of 2^32 + 2 reads as 2, a length of 2^31 as negative (SF-2); sverify clamps and raises
description: `SUBSTR` reads its start and length as 32-bit integers: `SUBSTR('hello', 4294967298, 1)` is `e` (start 2), `SUBSTR('hello', 4294967295, 1)` `o` (start -1, from the end), `SUBSTR('hello', 2, 2147483648)` and `SUBSTR('hello', 2, 3000000000)` `''` (negative lengths), `SUBSTR('hello', 2, 4294967297)` `e`. Nothing raises, where `POSITION` with a start past 2^31 raises. See [SF-2](../../../upstream/bugs/SF-2.json).
Strings are at most 128 MiB (exec-size-limits), so no start or length from 2^31 - 1 on can reach past one.
reference: `substring` raises outside `Text.substrInRange` (starts in `[-2^32, 2^32)`, lengths below 2^32) and otherwise takes what exists. sverify's SQL (`SnowflakeDialect.substring`, this PR) clamps starts and lengths to 2^31 - 1, raises for a start from 2^32 on, and refuses a literal length from 2^32 on (`writer-substring-int32`, `writer-substring-raise`).

provenance.checked_by: sverify_dev.probe_snowflake through the Snowflake CLI (Snowflake characterization session)

evidence.sql: SELECT substr('hello', 0, 2), substr('hello', 1, 2), substr('hello', -2), substr('hello', -2, 1), substr('hello', 2, -1), substr('hello', 2, 0), substr('hello', 9), substr('hello', -9, 3), substr('héllo', 2, 2), substr('hello', 4294967297, 1)

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_snowflake` runs each query through `snow sql` (Snowflake CLI 3.32.1) on an X-Small warehouse, Snowflake 10.40.102, with the session's `TIMEZONE` set to UTC and `USE_CACHED_RESULT` off; every other parameter is the account's default, recorded in the header of probes.json (`WEEK_START` 0, `WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY` 0, `DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING` LAST, `TIMESTAMP_TYPE_MAPPING` TIMESTAMP_NTZ). The inputs are literal `VALUES`, except the `sample-*` probes, which read TPC-H's LINEITEM (6,001,215 rows) in SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA.
